meta.scope: Chile batch 5 — International trade agreements / treaties (static + recurring citation) and deeper Banco Central de Chile institutional & policy layer. Completes the international and central-banking anchors.

candidates.title: Tratado Integral y Progresista de Asociación Transpacífico (CPTPP / TPP-11)
candidates.publisher: Estados Parte del CPTPP (Chile signatory and host of signing)
candidates.description: Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership. Signed in Santiago in 2018; in force for Chile since February 2023. High-standard mega-regional trade agreement covering goods, services, investment, intellectual property and regulatory cooperation among 11 (and expanding) Pacific-rim economies.
referenced_by: Chilean trade and export strategy documents
Central Bank and Ministry of Finance external-sector analysis
SUBREI and DIRECON publications on preferential market access
Business and academic assessments of Chile’s Asia-Pacific orientation
candidates.notes:
Prime mega-regional static + recurring-citation node — analogue of Mexico’s T-MEC and Argentina’s MERCOSUR.

Chile hosted the signing and was among the early ratifiers. The agreement deepens preferential access to Japan, Canada, Australia, Vietnam, Malaysia and others, and remains a living reference in Chilean trade policy and export-complex analysis. No separate ‘CPTPP statistical yearbook’ is required; continuous citation in trade and integration analysis satisfies the expanded node definition.

candidates.title: Tratado de Libre Comercio Chile–Estados Unidos
candidates.description: Bilateral free-trade agreement signed 2003, in force since 1 January 2004. Eliminates tariffs on substantially all bilateral trade and includes chapters on services, investment and intellectual property.
referenced_by: Chilean trade statistics and partner-share analysis
Central Bank balance-of-payments and trade commentary
Policy debates on US tariff actions and preferential access
candidates.notes: Long-standing bilateral FTA. Continuously cited whenever US market access, rules of origin or bilateral trade balances are discussed. Two decades of operation make it a stable reference instrument.

candidates.title: Tratado de Libre Comercio Chile–China
candidates.publisher: Gobierno de Chile / República Popular China
candidates.description: Bilateral free-trade agreement (Chile was the first Latin American country to sign an FTA with China). In force since 2006; has underpinned the rapid growth of bilateral trade, especially copper and agricultural exports.
referenced_by: Trade and copper-export analysis
Central Bank external-sector reports
Diplomatic and commercial anniversary assessments (20 years)
candidates.notes: Structurally important bilateral instrument. China is a top destination for Chilean copper and other exports; the FTA is routinely cited in explanations of the trade relationship and of Chile’s Asia strategy.

candidates.title: Acuerdo de Asociación / Acuerdo Marco Avanzado Chile–Unión Europea
candidates.description: Association Agreement (2002) modernised by the Advanced Framework Agreement and Interim Trade Agreement (in force from February 2025). Deepens goods, services and investment liberalisation and adds sustainability and geographical-indications provisions.
referenced_by: Chilean and EU trade-policy documents
Export-promotion material for the European market
Fiscal and external-sector analysis of preferential trade
candidates.notes: Major transatlantic instrument. The 2025 modernisation is already cited in official trade reporting. Static legal framework with continuous operational citation.

candidates.title: Alianza del Pacífico (Protocolo Comercial y marco institucional)
candidates.publisher: Estados miembros de la Alianza del Pacífico (Chile, Colombia, México, Perú)
candidates.description: Regional integration initiative among the four Pacific-facing Latin American economies. Commercial protocol and related instruments govern preferential trade, mobility and regulatory cooperation.
referenced_by: Chilean regional-integration and trade-policy documents
SUBREI reporting on Pacific Alliance initiatives
Comparative Latin American trade analysis
candidates.notes: Latin American Pacific counterpart to MERCOSUR. Continuously referenced in Chilean regional strategy and in discussions of deep integration among open Pacific economies.

candidates.title: Ley Orgánica Constitucional del Banco Central de Chile (Ley 18.840)
candidates.publisher: Poder Legislativo / Banco Central de Chile
candidates.description: Constitutional organic law (1989, subsequently amended) that establishes the Central Bank’s autonomy, objectives (currency stability and normal functioning of internal and external payments), governance and powers, including reserve management and monetary-policy instruments.
referenced_by: Every major BCCh policy and statistical publication
IPoM and financial-stability reports that cite the legal mandate
Academic and legal analyses of central-bank independence in Chile
candidates.notes: Foundational static + recurring-citation node for the Chilean central bank — direct analogue of Argentina’s BCRA legal framework and of Mexico’s Banco de México organic law. Continuously cited as the source of the inflation-targeting mandate and of the Bank’s statistical and reserve-management powers.

candidates.title: Informe de Política Monetaria (IPoM)
candidates.description: Quarterly Monetary Policy Report of the Central Bank. Explains the inflation outlook, the medium-term analytical framework and the implications for the policy interest rate. Statutory reporting obligation to the Senate and the Minister of Finance.
candidates.notes: Flagship policy communication product. Published after the March, June, September and December monetary-policy meetings. Central reference for inflation expectations and for the interpretation of the 3% inflation target.

candidates.title: Reservas Internacionales del Banco Central de Chile
candidates.description: Stock of international reserves managed by the Central Bank under the powers granted by the organic law. Published at high frequency and analysed in the Bank’s financial and external-sector reports.
candidates.notes: Key external-vulnerability and monetary-policy indicator. Portfolio composition and investment policy are publicly described; reserves appear in the balance of payments (change in reserve assets) and in the IIP.

candidates.title: Marco de metas de inflación (3%) y régimen de tipo de cambio flexible
candidates.description: Operational monetary-policy framework: inflation targeting centred on 3% annual CPI inflation, complemented by a flexible exchange-rate regime. Derived from the organic-law mandate to preserve the stability of the currency.
referenced_by: Every IPoM and monetary-policy decision statement
IPC and inflation analysis that refers to the target
Academic and market commentary on Chilean monetary policy
candidates.notes: Core policy-framework node. Continuously cited as the reference against which inflation outcomes and policy actions are evaluated. Static institutional commitment with high-frequency operational citation.

candidates.title: Unidad de Fomento (UF) y Unidad Tributaria Mensual (UTM)
candidates.publisher: Banco Central de Chile / Servicio de Impuestos Internos
candidates.description: Inflation-indexed units of account. The UF is adjusted daily with the IPC and is widely used in contracts, mortgages and financial instruments; the UTM is used for tax and administrative purposes.
candidates.notes: Distinctive Chilean institutional feature. The UF links the IPC directly into the financial and contractual system; its daily value is a high-frequency official statistic derived from the consumer-price index.

proposed_edges.basis: CPTPP preferential access is a recurring analytical dimension of Chilean merchandise-trade and export-strategy reporting.
proposed_edges.reference_period: continuous / at each major trade update

proposed_edges.basis: The Chile–China FTA underpins the large bilateral trade relationship, especially copper exports.
The US FTA is the legal basis for preferential bilateral trade flows that appear in the trade statistics.
The IPoM is a statutory reporting instrument required by the organic law.
Reserve management powers are granted by the organic law.
The inflation-targeting framework operationalises the organic-law mandate to preserve currency stability.
The UF is adjusted daily with the IPC.
The Monetary Policy Report analyses inflation outcomes against the IPC and the 3% target.
